items.title: PrivaKit – A zero-upload AI workspace in the browser via WebGPU
items.raw_excerpt:
Hi HN, I'm the builder.
I realized that using cloud AI APIs for sensitive workflows—like transcribing board meetings, OCRing employment contracts, or cleaning up ID photos—is a massive privacy liability.
So I built a client-side workspace using transformers.js, Whisper, and WebGPU. Everything runs locally. You can turn on Airplane Mode after the initial model load, and it still transcribes and extracts text perfectly.
To keep myself honest, I wrote a technical audit of how the data flows (or rather, doesn't flow). My only backend is a tiny 2-core node in Singapore running self-hosted Plausible analytics: [ https://gist.github.com/ygx2378/3275b333504c6a9def50ef531b54... ]
I'm still learning the ropes of browser-based memory management, so I'd love your feedback on how the models load on you

items.title: Study: The Logic Behind AI's Judgments of People
items.raw_excerpt: New study shows that modern AI systems don’t just process information, they systematically “judge” people in ways that resemble human trust, but with important differences. Like humans, they favor competence and integrity, yet they do so in a more rigid, rule-based, and often more extreme way. Crucially, their judgments can also be more consistently biased across demographic traits and vary significantly between models.

excerpt_i18n.en:
Recently, Jindie Shikong and the Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences jointly achieved a significant technological breakthrough—the RISC-V AI CPU chip K3 successfully runs the OpenHarmony 6.1 system, making it the world's first RISC-V architecture chip to support OpenHarmony 6.1. This marks the adaptation of RISC-V chips and the open-source HarmonyOS entering a new phase of full autonomy and dual open-source in both "chip + system."  

During this adaptation process, both parties leveraged their respective technical strengths and collaborated deeply:  
▲ The Institute of Software provided OpenHarmony system-level technical support, completing RISC-V architecture compatibility and core component porting.  
▲ Jindie Shikong handled the underlying hardware adaptation, driver development, and performance optimization for the K3 chip.  

This combination truly achieves full-stack autonomy from chip to system, providing a more secure and controllable solution for smart terminals, IoT, and other fields.  

OpenHarmony 6.1 is the Long-Term Support (LTS) version released by the OpenHarmony community. Compared to previous versions, its advantages include:  
▲ Up to 3 years of official maintenance support, ensuring long-term stable iteration and making it more suitable for deployment in enterprise production environments.  
▲ Significantly enhanced application development capabilities, supporting more refined application control and smoother dynamic effects.  
▲ Upgraded system-level functionality and multimedia experience, improving system perception.
excerpt_i18n.es: Recientemente, Jindie Shikong y el Instituto de Software de la Academia China de Ciencias han logrado un importante avance tecnológico: el chip RISC-V AI CPU K3 ha ejecutado con éxito el sistema OpenHarmony 6.1, convirtiéndose en el primer chip de arquitectura RISC-V del mundo compatible con la versión 6.1 de OpenHarmony. Esto marca que la adaptación entre los chips RISC-V y el sistema operativo de código abierto Harmony ha entrado oficialmente en una nueva etapa de "chip + sistema", completamente autónoma y de doble código abierto. Durante este proceso de adaptación, ambas partes aprovecharon sus respectivas ventajas técnicas y colaboraron en profundidad: el Instituto de Software proporcionó OpenHarmony.

An "unpretentious and straightforward" private gathering took place on the afternoon of April 11 at the Z·Pilot space in Nantou Ancient Town, Shenzhen, where 15 people spent four hours behind closed doors. There was no live streaming, no recording, no PowerPoint presentations, and no company introductions. The first words upon entering were "Who am I," followed immediately by speaking candidly.

This was the inaugural Conclave by HardTech Community—a closed-door meeting specifically designed for entrepreneurs in the sports technology sector. Attendees included creators of smart tennis robots, action cameras, skiing equipment, rehabilitation medical devices, and several investors. None of the usual talk from product launches was heard here.

What is HardTech Community? It is an investor community under Leiphone, focusing on hard tech sectors like AI hardware, robotics, and smart mobility. We don’t host large conferences or pitch events—we do one thing: bring together those truly immersed in these fields for an afternoon of candid conversation.

HardTech Conclave is a series of closed-door meetings jointly organized by Leiphone’s HardTech Community and investment institutions. Each session strictly limits attendance to 15 or fewer, inviting only participants with genuine entrepreneurial experience or deep industry insights. No company introductions, no business card exchanges—just discussions on insights and challenges.

The co-organizer, Different Capital, originates from a family office of one of Alibaba’s founders, focusing on cross-border e-commerce, AI software and hardware, and robotics. They have invested in companies like Walker Extraordinary, Inhands Power, DeepGaze Technology, and Squirrel Power, and possess a systematic framework for evaluating the sports hardware sector.

excerpt_i18n.en:
Author | Wu You  Editor | Yu Kuai  
Imagine a specific scenario: you wake up at 9 a.m., open your phone, and find 47 notifications piled up from over a dozen apps. Checking and handling them one by one is time-consuming and makes it easy to miss the key points.  

At this moment, a hardware product called YoooClaw comes into play. It integrates information across applications, automatically organizing it into a tiered board categorized as urgent, to be handled, or for awareness only, making information clear at a glance. It also incorporates AI capabilities to deeply analyze the impact of information, directly providing users with actionable suggestions. YoooClaw helps users transform chaotic notification streams into clear decision-making flows, allowing them to see at first glance what needs to be handled most urgently each day, becoming their most capable action partner.  

Unlike other products such as Plaud, YoooClaw does not gather user context through chat interfaces or build user memory through recordings. Instead, it refines scattered, noisy information from users’ daily behaviors—such as notifications, cross-application actions, fragmented tasks, and lightweight records—into personal context, organizing it into more valuable inputs. This makes AI more useful in real-world scenarios.  

YoooClaw’s founder, Xiao Ruizhe, co-founded the open-source website-building software PHPWind while studying at Beijing Jiaotong University, which was later acquired by Alibaba. After joining Alibaba, he participated in the entire lifecycle of Alibaba Cloud OS, from its establishment to its integration into Banma. He later joined Huawei’s Smart Selection Car team, deeply involved in product definition, pricing, target audience, and gross margin calculations.
